h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבָּת תְּשׁוּבָה, א׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 1
"And Moshe Went": A Goer Who Rises from Level to Level

p: such wording anywhere in the Torah.
But the matter is based on
"This teaches that each and every tzaddik
has a world of his own
(and so it is written in the Midrash Rabbah,
And all of a person's days
in this world he is called a "goer."
between an angel and a man,
"I will give you places to walk
for an angel is called "one who stands,"
which is not so with man:
This is why it says "And Moshe went":
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
this level of which he said
"I can no longer go out and come in";
"For a tzaddik falls seven times and rises";
that is, in the manner of
"a descent that is for the sake of an ascent."
This is "For a tzaddik falls seven times" —
since it is for the sake of ascent.
and this is the final level.
This is why it says here "And Moshe went":
And all the parshiyos from here
to the end of the Torah that were said

paragraphs.text: Commentary: Ibn Ezra on Devarim 31:1 — “‘And he went’: he went to each and every tribe to let them know that he was dying, so that they would not be afraid, and he strengthened their hearts with the words of Yehoshua… and in my opinion it was then that he blessed the tribes, even though their blessings are written later.” Connection: Ibn Ezra answers the plain question of where Moshe went; the maamar takes the unusual word “vayeilech” inward, as the motion of one who goes from level to level.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 283b (Vayeilech) — "'And Moshe went' — where did he go? Rather, he 'went' like a body without an arm, as you say, 'And they went without strength before the pursuer' (Eichah 1:6); for Aharon, the right arm, had died, and the body sought to depart. All the days of Moshe, the sun shone in the world."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 152a — "'For man goes to his eternal home' (Koheles 12:5). Rabbi Yitzchak said: This teaches that each and every tzaddik is given a dwelling according to his honor. A parable: a king entered a city with his servants. When they enter, they all enter by one gate; when they lodge, each is given a dwelling according to his honor."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 1 — “The second Shabbos comes with greater holiness than the Shabbos before it. All a person's days are so: the weekdays are journeying and walking in the service of Hashem, and when Shabbos comes, rest comes, for then he is in the aspect of rest; as it says, ‘For man goes to his eternal home’ (Koheles 12:5), and in the Gemara (Shabbos 152a), each tzaddik has a dwelling of his own.” Connection: Rav Tzadok elsewhere joins the same Gemara on “going” to the tzaddik's own dwelling with the ascent of each Shabbos, the key to “And Moshe went.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'aloscha 1 — “Between level and level there is a journey, in which he goes and travels to reach that level, and then he is in turmoil; and when he reaches the level he is at rest. And this is all of man all the days of his life: in the days of action he is in turmoil, and that is preparation to come to Shabbos.” Connection: Both describe man in this world as one who keeps going from level to level.

paragraphs.text: Makkos 7b — "Rabbi Abahu asked Rabbi Yochanan: If he was going up a ladder and a rung slipped out from under him, fell and killed — what is the law? … He said to him: You have already touched on a descent that is for the sake of an ascent."
